title: Claude Code hooks: every event, with examples to copy
summary: Claude Code hooks run your scripts at set points in a session. See all 33 events, how exit codes control Claude, and four example hooks.
body_markdown:
Claude Code hooks are commands, HTTP calls, MCP tool calls, prompts or subagents that Claude Code runs automatically at set points in a session: before a tool call, after it, when Claude finishes responding, and 30 more events. You define them in a settings file, they fire every time their event happens, and their exit code or JSON output can block the action, send Claude feedback, or add context.


That makes hooks the place for rules that must hold every time. A line in CLAUDE.md is context that Claude reads and interprets. A hook is code that Claude Code runs on its own, so the action happens whether or not the model thinks of it. Anthropic's[hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide) calls this deterministic control.


Hook events and settings here follow Anthropic's docs as of Oct 12, 2026. If you're setting up Claude Code for a team, start with our[practical guide to using Claude Code](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/how-to-use-claude-code) .


## How a Claude Code hook works


Every hook has three layers:


1.


Event: the moment it fires, such as` PreToolUse` or` Stop` .


2.


Matcher: a filter on when it fires, such as "only the Bash tool".


3.


Handlers: what runs when the event and matcher line up.


Handlers come in five types:


-


` command` runs a shell command. It receives the event as JSON on stdin and answers through its exit code, stdout and stderr.


-


` http` sends the same JSON as a POST request and reads the response body.


-


` mcp_tool` calls a tool on an MCP server you've configured.


-


` prompt` sends the input to a Claude model, which returns a decision as JSON. Use it for checks that need judgment.


-


` agent` starts a subagent that can read files before it decides. Anthropic marks agent hooks as experimental.


Per Anthropic's[features overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview) , a hook adds nothing to Claude's context unless it returns output, so a formatter that runs after every edit costs no context. For instructions that never change, a line in CLAUDE.md is simpler than a script; our guide to[CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-md-agents-md) covers how those files load.


## Every Claude Code hook event


Anthropic's[hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) lists 33 events as of Oct 12, 2026. A few run once per session (` SessionStart` ,` SessionEnd` ), a few once per turn (` UserPromptSubmit` ,` Stop` ,` StopFailure` ), and` PreToolUse` and` PostToolUse` run on every tool call. "Can block" means exit code 2, or a blocking JSON decision, stops the action.


Event


When it fires


Can block?


` SessionStart`


A session starts or resumes


No


` Setup`


Claude Code starts with` --init-only` , or with` --init` or` --maintenance` in` -p` mode


No


` InstructionsLoaded`


A CLAUDE.md or` .claude/rules/*.md` file loads into context


No


` UserPromptSubmit`


You submit a prompt, before Claude processes it


Yes, rejects the prompt


` UserPromptExpansion`


A command you typed expands into a prompt


Yes, blocks the expansion


` PreToolUse`


Before a tool call runs


Yes, blocks the call


` PermissionRequest`


A tool call needs a permission decision


Through JSON only (allow or deny)


` PermissionDenied`


Auto mode denies a tool call


No (JSON can allow a retry)


` PostToolUse`


After a tool call succeeds


No, but stderr reaches Claude


` PostToolUseFailure`


After a tool call fails


No, but stderr reaches Claude


` PostToolBatch`


After a batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call


Yes, stops the loop


` Notification`


Claude Code sends a notification


No


` MessageDisplay`


While Claude's message text is displayed


No (can change the displayed text)


` SubagentStart`


A subagent is spawned


No


` SubagentStop`


A subagent finishes


Yes, keeps it working


` TaskCreated`


A task is created with` TaskCreate`


Yes, cancels the task


` TaskCompleted`


A task is being marked complete


Yes, keeps it open


` TeammateIdle`


An agent team teammate is about to go idle


Yes, keeps it working


` Stop`


Claude finishes responding


Yes, keeps Claude working


` StopFailure`


A turn ends because of an API error


No


` PreCompact`


Before context compaction


Yes


` PostCompact`


After compaction completes


No


` PreModelSwitch`


Before a model switch you or a client requested


Yes


` PostModelSwitch`


After the session's model changes


No


` ConfigChange`


A configuration file changes during the session


Yes, except policy settings


` CwdChanged`


The working directory changes


No


` DirectoryAdded`


A directory is added with` /add-dir` or the SDK


No


` FileChanged`


A file you told it to watch changes on disk


No


` WorktreeCreate`


A worktree is created; the hook replaces the default git behavior


Yes, any non-zero exit fails it


` WorktreeRemove`


A worktree is removed


Yes, a non-zero exit fails the removal


` Elicitation`


An MCP server asks for user input during a tool call


Yes, denies the request


` ElicitationResult`


After you answer an MCP elicitation, before the answer goes back


Yes


` SessionEnd`


The session ends


No


Matchers filter on a different field for each event. Tool events match the tool name, such as` Bash` ,` Edit|Write` or` mcp__github__.*` .` SessionStart` matches how the session began (` startup` ,` resume` ,` clear` ,` compact` or` fork` ).` SubagentStart` and` SubagentStop` match the subagent's name, and` Notification` matches the notification type, such as` permission_prompt` or` idle_prompt` .` UserPromptSubmit` ,` Stop` ,` PostToolBatch` ,` TeammateIdle` ,` TaskCreated` ,` TaskCompleted` ,` WorktreeCreate` ,` WorktreeRemove` ,` MessageDisplay` and` CwdChanged` don't take a matcher and fire every time.


## Where hooks are configured


Hooks live in JSON settings files and a few other places, including[plugins](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-plugins) and[skills](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-skills) . Where you put one sets its scope:


Location


Scope


Shared with the team?


` ~/.claude/settings.json`


All your projects


No, local to your machine


` .claude/settings.json`


One project


Yes, commit it to the repo


` .claude/settings.local.json`


One project


No, Claude Code gitignores it when it saves a setting there


Managed policy settings


Whole organization


Yes, set by admins


A plugin's` hooks/hooks.json`


While the plugin is enabled


Yes, ships with the plugin


Skill frontmatter


Rest of the session once the skill is invoked


Yes, in the skill file


Subagent frontmatter


While that subagent runs


Yes, in the subagent file


A few rules about how these combine:


-


Hooks from every level merge. A project hook doesn't replace a user hook, and a handler defined in two settings files runs once.


-


Claude Code normally picks up edits to settings files on its own, and` /hooks` lists every hook and where it came from.


-


To pause all hooks, set` "disableAllHooks": true` . There is no switch for one hook, and only managed settings can turn off managed hooks.


-


Cloud sessions don't read your local` ~/.claude/settings.json` .


-


Settings, managed and plugin hooks also run inside subagents, with` agent_id` and` agent_type` in the input. A subagent's own frontmatter hooks run only while it's active; our[subagents guide](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-subagents) uses one to keep a reviewer read-only.


### The shape of a hook entry


Each event name is a key inside one` hooks` object. Under it sits a list of matcher groups, and each group holds a list of handlers. This one, from Anthropic's reference, runs a lint script after Claude writes or edits a file:


```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{
"matcher"  :    "Edit|Write"  ,
"hooks"  :    [
{
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "/path/to/lint-check.sh"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{
"matcher"  :    "Edit|Write"  ,
"hooks"  :    [
{
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "/path/to/lint-check.sh"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{
"matcher"  :    "Edit|Write"  ,
"hooks"  :    [
{
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "/path/to/lint-check.sh"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


If your settings file already has a` hooks` key, add new events as siblings inside it rather than a second` hooks` object.


### Matchers and the` if` field


-


` "*"` ,` ""` or no matcher at all matches everything.


-


A matcher made only of letters, digits,` _` ,` -` , spaces, commas and` |` is an exact match or a list of them, so` Edit|Write` matches either tool.


-


Anything else is a JavaScript regular expression, and it isn't anchored:` Edit.*` also matches` NotebookEdit` . Write` ^Edit$` when you need a whole-name match.


-


Matchers are case-sensitive. MCP tools are named` mcp__<server>__<tool>` , so` mcp__memory__.*` matches every tool from the` memory` server.


On tool events you can narrow further with the` if` field. It takes one permission rule, such as` "Bash(git *)"` or` "Edit(*.ts)"` , and the handler only spawns when the tool call matches. For Bash, each subcommand is checked, so` Bash(git *)` fires on` npm test && git push` . Anthropic calls` if` best-effort and recommends[permission rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) , not hooks, for a hard allow or deny.


### Pointing at scripts


Use` ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` for the project root, or` ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` inside a plugin. Anthropic recommends setting` args` (an argument list, even an empty one) whenever a command uses one of these placeholders: Claude Code then runs the executable directly with no shell, each argument is passed as is, and paths with spaces need no quoting. The examples below also use` timeout` , in seconds (600 by default for command hooks on most events), and` statusMessage` , the spinner text while the hook runs.


## What a hook receives


A command hook gets one JSON object on stdin. The common fields are:


-


` session_id` and` prompt_id`


-


` transcript_path` , the path to the conversation file


-


` cwd` , the directory Claude is working in


-


` permission_mode` , such as` default` ,` plan` ,` acceptEdits` or` auto` (most events)


-


` hook_event_name`


-


` agent_id` and` agent_type` , when the hook fires inside a subagent


Each event adds its own fields. A` PreToolUse` hook for a Bash call receives something like this:


```text

"session_id"  :    "abc123"  ,
"transcript_path"  :    "/home/user/.claude/projects/.../transcript.jsonl"  ,
"cwd"  :    "/home/user/my-project"  ,
"permission_mode"  :    "default"  ,
"hook_event_name"  :    "PreToolUse"  ,
"tool_name"  :    "Bash"  ,
"tool_input"  :    {
"command"  :    "npm test"  ,
"description"  :    "Run test suite"
}  ,
"tool_use_id"  :    "toolu_01ABC123..."
}
```

For scripts that read this input:


-


For` Write` ,` Edit` and` Read` ,` tool_input.file_path` is always absolute. Claude Code expands` ~` and relative paths first, so a path check can't be dodged with a different spelling.


-


` Stop` hooks get` stop_hook_active` , which is` true` when Claude is already continuing because a Stop hook blocked it, and` last_assistant_message` , the text of Claude's final reply. Read that rather than the transcript file, which is written asynchronously and can lag.


## How exit codes and output control Claude


The exit code is the simplest signal:


Exit code


Meaning


What Claude Code does


0


Success


Proceeds and reads any JSON on stdout. Plain stdout goes to the debug log, except on` UserPromptSubmit` ,` UserPromptExpansion` ,` SessionStart` and` PostModelSwitch` , where Claude gets it as context


2


Block


On events that can block, stops the action. The message is your stderr, or your JSON's reason; for a blocked tool call or` Stop` , Claude reads it


Anything else


Non-blocking error (most events)


Proceeds and shows a` hook error` notice with the first line of stderr


On most events, exit code 1, the usual Unix failure code, doesn't block, so a policy hook should exit 2. And a hook that can't start, because the path is wrong or the script isn't executable, also lands in the non-blocking bucket. A typo in` settings.json` quietly turns your gate off, so watch for a hook error notice the first time a new hook runs. On Claude Code v2.1.295 or later, setting` "onFailure": "block"` on a command or HTTP hook makes a hook that can't start, times out or exits with an unexpected code block the action instead; it has no effect on` Stop` hooks.


### JSON output for finer control


When block-or-allow isn't enough, exit 0 and print a JSON object on stdout. Pick one approach per hook: exit codes alone, or exit 0 plus JSON. On events that can block, exit 2 wins even if your JSON says allow.


-


Universal fields work on most events.` "continue": false` stops Claude entirely and shows the user` stopReason` , and` systemMessage` shows the user a warning.


-


` decision` and` reason` let events such as` UserPromptSubmit` ,` PostToolUse` ,` Stop` and` SubagentStop` block or send feedback. The only value for` decision` is` "block"` .


-


` hookSpecificOutput` carries richer control and needs a` hookEventName` . On` PreToolUse` it holds` permissionDecision` (` allow` ,` deny` ,` ask` or` defer` ) with a` permissionDecisionReason` , and` updatedInput` can rewrite the tool's arguments. On several events it can hold` additionalContext` , text Claude reads as a system reminder.


This denies a tool call and tells Claude why:


```text
{
"hookSpecificOutput"  :    {
"hookEventName"  :    "PreToolUse"  ,
"permissionDecision"  :    "deny"  ,
"permissionDecisionReason"  :    "Database writes are not allowed"
}
}
```


```text
{
"hookSpecificOutput"  :    {
"hookEventName"  :    "PreToolUse"  ,
"permissionDecision"  :    "deny"  ,
"permissionDecisionReason"  :    "Database writes are not allowed"
}
}
```


```text
{
"hookSpecificOutput"  :    {
"hookEventName"  :    "PreToolUse"  ,
"permissionDecision"  :    "deny"  ,
"permissionDecisionReason"  :    "Database writes are not allowed"
}
}
```


Write` additionalContext` as plain facts ("This repo uses` bun test` "), not as commands. Anthropic notes that text framed as system instructions can trip Claude's prompt-injection defenses. Each` additionalContext` ,` systemMessage` and plain stdout value is capped at 10,000 characters.


Hooks also sit above permission modes. A` PreToolUse` hook that returns` deny` blocks the tool even in` bypassPermissions` mode, but one that returns` allow` can't override a deny rule in your settings.


## Four example Claude Code hooks


These are examples to adapt. The first two follow Anthropic's guide; the test gate and review hook are our own, so try each one in a scratch repo before you rely on it. Each goes in` .claude/settings.json` , so the whole team gets it. The scripts parse JSON with` jq` , so install it first. Save scripts under` .claude/hooks/` and run` chmod +x` on them, or they fail without blocking anything.


### 1. Format every file Claude edits


A` PostToolUse` hook with an` Edit|Write` matcher runs after each file edit. This one, from Anthropic's guide, passes the edited path to Prettier:


```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{
"matcher"  :    "Edit|Write"  ,
"hooks"  :    [
{
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{

"hooks"  :    [

"command"  :    "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write"
}
]

```

```text
{
"hooks"  :    {
"PostToolUse"  :    [
{
"matcher"  :    "Edit|Write"  ,
"hooks"  :    [
{
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


When it works, you see nothing in the conversation; the file is just formatted. Swap in the formatter your project uses.` PostToolUse` can't undo the edit, and the matcher only sees the Edit and Write tools. To catch a specific file however it changes, including a Bash rewrite, use a` FileChanged` hook.


### 2. Block edits to sensitive files


A` PreToolUse` hook runs before the edit, so it can stop it. This script, adapted from Anthropic's guide, exits 2 when the target path matches a protected pattern, and Claude gets the message as feedback. Unlike the original, it fails closed: without` jq` , it blocks the edit.


```text
#!/bin/bash
# Example: .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh
INPUT  = $(cat)


# Fail closed: without jq this guard can't read the path.
command  -v   jq >/dev/null || {  echo    "protect-files.sh needs jq to check paths"   >&2;  exit    2  ; }


FILE_PATH  = $(echo   "  $INPUT  "   | jq -r   '.tool_input.file_path // empty'  )


# Normalize Windows backslashes so the patterns match
FILE_PATH  = "  ${FILE_PATH//\\//}  "


PROTECTED_PATTERNS  =( ".env"    "package-lock.json"    ".git/"  )


for   pattern  in    "  ${PROTECTED_PATTERNS[@]}  "  ;  do
if   [[  "  $FILE_PATH  "   == * "  $pattern  "  * ]];  then
echo    "Blocked:   $FILE_PATH   matches protected pattern '  $pattern  '"   >&2
exit    2
fi
done


exit    0
```

### 3. Run tests before Claude stops


` Stop` fires when Claude finishes responding. Exit 2 from a Stop hook keeps Claude working and hands it your stderr as the reason. That gives you a test gate: if tests fail, Claude fixes them before handing the turn back to you.


```text
#!/bin/bash
# Example: .claude/hooks/test-gate.sh
INPUT  = $(cat)


# Without jq the loop guard below can't work, so let Claude stop.
command  -v   jq >/dev/null ||  exit    0


CWD  = $(jq -r   '.cwd'   <<<  "  $INPUT  "  )
ROOT  = $(git -C   "  $CWD  "   rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)   ||  exit    0
cd    "  $ROOT  "   ||  exit    0


# Stop fires after every response. Skip the run when nothing has changed.
[  -z    "  $(git status --porcelain)  "   ] &&  exit    0


if    OUTPUT  = $(npm test 2>&1)  ;  then
exit    0
fi


# Claude already had one retry. Let it stop, and warn the user.
if   [  "  $(jq -r   '.stop_hook_active'   <<<  "  $INPUT  "  )  "   =  "true"   ];  then
jq  -nc    '{systemMessage: "Tests still fail after one retry. Check them before you merge."}'
exit    0
fi


{
echo    "Tests are failing. Fix them before you finish. Last 40 lines:"
tail  -n    40   <<< "  $OUTPUT  "
} >&2
exit    2
```

```text
"type"  :    "command"  ,
"command"  :    "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/test-gate.sh"  ,
"args"  :    [  ]  ,
"timeout"  :    300  ,
"statusMessage"  :    "Running tests before Claude finishes"
}
]
}
]
}
}
```


Replace` npm test` with your test command. How it behaves:


-


` Stop` fires after every response, not only at the end of a task, so the script skips the run when the working tree is clean.


-


The first failure blocks and sends Claude the last 40 lines of output. If tests still fail at the next stop,` stop_hook_active` is` true` , so the script lets Claude stop and warns you through` systemMessage` instead of looping. Claude Code also ends the turn itself after Stop hooks block eight times in a row with no tool call in between.


-


It fails safe: without` jq` or outside a git repo it lets Claude stop, and if the suite runs past the hook's` timeout` , Claude Code cancels the hook and the turn ends as if nothing blocked.


### 4. Review the diff before every commit


Claude Code wrote 78.1% of the AI-written code that cubic reviewed in the latest full week, according to[Bug Bench](https://www.cubic.dev/bugbench/harnesses/claude-code) . That share covers code reviewed by cubic, not the whole market. A` PreToolUse` hook on` git commit` puts a review in front of each commit Claude makes, while Claude still has the context to fix what it finds.


This example calls cubic's CLI as its[docs](https://docs.cubic.dev/ide/cli-review) describe it.
```text
#!/bin/bash
# Example: .claude/hooks/review-before-commit.sh
INPUT  = $(cat)
COMMAND  = $(jq -r   '.tool_input.command // empty'   <<<  "  $INPUT  "  )


# The if filter is best-effort, so check the command here too.
[[  "  $COMMAND  "   == * "git commit"  * ]] ||  exit    0


REPORT  = $(cubic review --json 2>/dev/null)
COUNT  = $(jq   '.issues | length'   <<<  "  $REPORT  "   2>/dev/null)


# Block only on a positive issue count. Anything else fails open.
if   [[  "  $COUNT  "   =~ ^[1-9][0-9]* $   ]];  then
{
echo    "Review found   $COUNT   issue(s) in the uncommitted changes."
echo    "Fix them, then commit again. If you think a finding is wrong, stop and ask the user instead of committing."
jq  '.issues'   <<< "  $REPORT  "
} >&2
exit    2
fi


exit    0
```

The wrapper exists because the CLI exits with code 1 when it reports findings, and Claude Code treats exit code 1 from a hook as a non-blocking error, so every commit would go through. The script exits 2 instead, which blocks the commit and hands Claude the findings. How it handles trouble:


-


It fails open. If` jq` or the CLI is missing, or the review errors out, the commit goes ahead. Add an` exit 2` for an empty report if you'd rather fail closed.


-


Command hooks time out after 600 seconds by default, and a timed-out` PreToolUse` hook doesn't block. Raise` timeout` if your reviews take longer.


-


The message tells Claude to stop and ask you when it disagrees with a finding, so a disputed finding doesn't turn into a loop.


With another review tool, keep the wrapper and swap the command: exit 2 with the findings on stderr when the commit should wait.


A local review is a first pass. cubic's docs recommend its GitHub pull request review as the final one, since that review uses a different model and pipeline and may find issues the CLI misses. Our guide to[AI code review](https://www.cubic.dev/ai-code-review) covers where each step fits, and[a pre-review safety gate for AI-generated code](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/a-pre-review-safety-gate-for-ai-generated-code) covers gating agent output. For the whole loop in Claude Code, from a local review to fixing pull request comments, see our[Claude Code review guide](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/code-review-in-claude-code) .


## Security: hooks run with your permissions


Command hooks run with your full user permissions. They can read, change or delete anything your account can, so review every hook before you add it, especially one from a repo you didn't write.


Workspace trust adds a guard in interactive sessions: Claude Code holds back hooks from settings files until you accept the trust dialog for the folder. A` claude -p` or Agent SDK session treats the folder as trusted, so hooks committed in a repo's` .claude/settings.json` run without asking. Before you script` claude -p` over someone else's repository, read its` .claude/` settings, or turn hooks off for that run with` --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` .


Anthropic's checklist for hook scripts: validate input, quote shell variables (` "$VAR"` ), reject paths that contain` ..` , use absolute paths, and skip sensitive files such as` .env` and keys.


## Debugging a hook that doesn't fire


-


Run` /hooks` and check that the hook is listed under the right event.


-


Check the matcher. Matchers are case-sensitive.


-


Run the script by hand with sample input:` echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | ./my-hook.sh; echo $?`


-


If your JSON output has no effect, look for a shell profile that prints text on startup. Anything printed before the` {` makes Claude Code treat the whole output as plain text.


-


Start Claude Code with` claude --debug-file /tmp/claude.log` to log which hooks matched, their exit codes and their output, or run` /debug` to turn logging on mid-session.


## FAQ


### Which exit code blocks an action in a Claude Code hook?


Exit code 2. On events that can block, such as` PreToolUse` ,` UserPromptSubmit` and` Stop` , it stops the action, and for a tool call or` Stop` , Claude gets your stderr as the reason. On most events, exit code 1 and other non-zero codes are non-blocking errors, so the action goes ahead. You can also block by exiting 0 with a JSON decision, such as` "permissionDecision": "deny"` on` PreToolUse` .


### What is the difference between hooks and mods in Claude Code?


The hooks in this guide are configured in settings. A mod is a plugin that registers hooks as JavaScript functions, which Claude Code calls in its own process, and it can also draw in the interface. Both work side by side, but a mod that handles` tool.check` can approve a call your` PreToolUse` hook blocked, unless that hook lives in managed settings.


### How do I get a notification when Claude Code needs input?


Add a` Notification` hook to` ~/.claude/settings.json` . On macOS, Anthropic's guide uses the command` osascript -e 'display notification "Claude Code needs your attention" with title "Claude Code"'` . Use a matcher such as` permission_prompt` or` idle_prompt` to limit which notifications trigger it. For a terminal notification that also works in tmux, return the escape sequence in the` terminalSequence` JSON field instead of writing to` /dev/tty` .
